Hello!

Thank you for this wonderful package again.

I was recently analyzing IGT behavior data and using hBayesDM for computational modeling. I have successfully finished the igt_orl, igt_pvl_decay, igt_pvl_delta, igt_vpp model fitting and model comparison. But I still have some questions.

1. The model fits were assessed using the LOOIC and WAIC, but how to do simulation for each model?  (like the below figures)

2. My experiment is 2*2*2 mixed-design, can I directly perform ANOVA or t-test on the model parameters?


3. The resulting A(learning rate) in igt_vpp is very low, is this low value normal?




Best,

Xuerui

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Questions about model simulation and group comparison
parts:
Hi Xuerui,

Thanks for your interest! For your questions: 

(1) While hBayesDM does not currently do simulations out-of-the-box, our recent IGT paper (citation below) has some code online that you may be able to adapt to do the simulation (see: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/IGT). If you download the linked dropbox folder, the "R/1_analysis/1_Simulation" directory contains the code that I wrote to do simulations from the respective paper. You would likely need to make some modifications, but it should be a useful start.

(2) For comparing parameters, it is not best practice to run frequentist tests on the posterior parameter estimates (because they reduce posterior distributions to point estimates). We recommend that you directly compare the parameters as described in the tutorial paper (see: https://www.mitpressjournals.org/doi/full/10.1162/CPSY_a_00002). An alternative strategy would be to construct different models which assume specific sets of parameters differ between groups/conditions and then use model comparison to determine which model best explains the data. For this, you would need to modify the Stan codes directly. 

(3) In my experience, that is not too low of a number. However, it can be useful to look at the whole group-level posterior distribution (and even individual-level parameters) to see if things look OK. I actually have a blog post with some accompanying R code that shows how  different learning rates affect trial-by-trial estimates of expected value (see: http://haines-lab.com/post/2017-04-04-choice_rl_1/)—feel free to play around with the code to gain an intuition for how to interpret the learning rates! 

I hope this can be helpful. 

Best,
Nate


IGT Citation: 
Haines, N., Vassileva, J., & Ahn, W. Y. (2018). The Outcome‐Representation Learning Model: A Novel Reinforcement Learning Model of the Iowa Gambling Task. Cognitive science, 42(8), 2534-2561.

Dear Nate,

Thanks for your reply! It’s very helpful. However, I still have some questions.

(1) For group comparison in a Bayesian way, it usually comparing between two groups. But my experiment is 2*2*2 design with two within subjects factors and one between subjects factor. So  how to test the main effects of the factors and the interactions? 

(2) Each subjects performed IGT twice (the decks is the same), should I change the prior probability in the second measure?

Best,

Xuerui

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: Questions about model simulation and group comparison
parts:
Hi Xuerui,

Thanks for your email, but I think this is beyond the scope of what we can do for hBayesDM users. Typically, for within-subject comparisons, you would need to tweak Stan codes on your own. Regarding the choice of prior, I think it depends on the assumption you would make.

Best,
Young
